intro: A calendar of freedoms handed over by age, unconditionally — adapted from Ken Wilgus's Planned Emancipation (Feeding the Mouth That Bites You). A privilege is "I'll be nice and let you." A freedom is "it's no longer up to me."
rules: It never comes back — never revoked as punishment.
Boundaries exist only to protect everyone else, not because you dislike the choice.

sortingTest.question: Could I actually enforce this if they decided otherwise?

answers.answer: No (music, clothes, friends, beliefs, free time)
answers.verdict: Track B calendar — gating it is a fiction that costs influence.

answers.answer: Yes, with physical or financial stakes (driving, credit card, home alone)

rows.title: Your own space & taste
freedoms: How your room is decorated and kept
rows.notes: Boundaries only where it touches others: shared spaces stay shared, family events may have a dress code.

rows.title: Your own time & people
freedoms: How you spend your discretionary money
rows.notes: We can tell you what we see in a friendship; we no longer pick your friends.

rows.title: Your own work
rows.notes: Grades are yours to earn and own. Social media within the law and with safety boundaries that protect others.

rows.title: Your own choices
rows.notes: The dating age is a family decision — set it on purpose, announce it early. Earned money needs somewhere to live: if the bank-account skill hasn't happened yet, this freedom arrives with an account to hold it.

rows.title: Your own convictions
rows.notes: The faith rows are the family's to set. The goal was never attendance — it was ownership.

rows.title: Everything
rows.notes: By the declared adulthood date, there is nothing left to hand over — that's the point.

companions.expectations: Alongside freedoms, keep a written Expectations & Consequences list in video-camera terms: if you filmed them meeting the expectation, what would you see? Consequences touch privileges, never transferred freedoms.
companions.adulthoodDate: Declare an adulthood date and tell the kid years in advance. Everything in both tracks counts down to it.
